verses.note: The sea stays within the limits God sets. Later Scripture uses this as a picture of God's continuing rule over every power that threatens life (Psalm 104:9, Jeremiah 5:22), and the Gospels show Jesus rebuking the wind and the sea.

Creation works through secondary causes, the earth bringing forth, without ceasing to be God's direct work. The Bible sees no rivalry between saying that the land produces life and saying that God makes it.
Before humanity does anything, God gives. The first word of provision in the Bible establishes that life is received as gift, the pattern Jesus teaches in the prayer for daily bread.

The list is a record of a promise kept. God had said he would make Ishmael a great nation (Genesis 17:20, 21:18), and Genesis takes the space to show it, even for a line that will leave the main story after verse 18.

God protects the promised mother through the conscience of a Philistine king. No plague or dream is needed; God works through ordinary moral sense in people outside the covenant family, and the story does not flatter the covenant family by comparison.

Isaac does not win the wells by force; he yields until God gives room. The verse names God as the one who makes space for his people in a hostile land, a confession that recurs in the Psalms: "In my distress I called to the LORD", and the Hebrew goes on to say that he answered in a broad place (Psalm 118:5).

Even Rebekah's half-truth serves God's purpose. Jacob's flight will take him to Haran, to his wives, to the births of the twelve tribes' ancestors, and to a meeting with God at Bethel on the road (28:10-22).

The son who stole the blessing is now sent away with his father's blessing and orders. What began as flight from Esau becomes, by Isaac's word, a mission to find a wife, and the chapter will show God himself taking charge of the road.

Each verb is a promise of God's active care: to be with, to guard, to bring back, not to abandon. Jacob will quote the promise back to God when he is afraid of Esau (32:9-12), and at the end of his life he describes God as the one who shepherded him all his life (48:15).
